planting.note: Start indoors under warm conditions and transplant after all frost danger has passed; AuDrey is a basal-branching series bred for uniform habit in gallon containers as well as cut-flower production.

directions: Sow indoors on a heat mat, since Gomphrena germinates best at consistently warm soil temperatures, then transplant into full sun once nights stay reliably above 60°F. AuDrey produces strong basal branching for a tidier, more self-supporting plant than older tall cutting types, holding its round papery flower heads in purple-red, pink, bicolor rose, or white well above the foliage. It shrugs off Gulf Coast heat and humidity and keeps flowering with little supplemental water once roots are established. Pinching young plants once encourages fuller branching for garden beds, while unpinched plants develop the longer stems preferred for fresh and dried cutting.
sources: North Carolina State University Extension Cut Flower Trials

planting.note: Start indoors and transplant after danger of frost has passed; Las Vegas is a compact, uniform bedding series noticeably shorter than cut-flower gomphrena types, suited to borders and containers.

directions: Transplant into well-drained, full-sun beds only after the soil has warmed, since Las Vegas grows slowly in cool conditions and accelerates once summer heat arrives. This compact series stays low and mounded compared to taller cutting types, making it a dependable filler for edging, mixed containers, and mass bedding in white, pink, or purple. Plants tolerate drought and reflected heat well once established and need only occasional watering during prolonged dry spells. Deadheading is not necessary, as the papery flower heads persist and continue to look tidy through the summer into fall.
sources: North Carolina State University Extension Cut Flower Trials

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; Ping Pong produces unusually round, uniform flower heads in white, lavender, and purple prized for their perfectly spherical shape.

directions: Transplant into lean, well-drained soil in full sun after frost danger has passed, since rich soil favors foliage over flowering. Ping Pong's flower heads are more perfectly round than most globe amaranth selections, resembling small solid balls held on sturdy stems above dark green foliage, which makes them especially popular for uniform bouquets and everlasting dried arrangements. Plants tolerate heat, humidity, and drought with ease and bloom continuously from early summer through the first hard frost. Cut stems for drying as soon as the heads fully color and hang them upside down in a dark, airy spot to preserve their shape and hue.
